text:
maria: quick one — PR #4821 adds new cross-lang examples for streaming + pagination + retry semantics. need a short review, esp the Go cursor example and the python async generator wording.

leo: looking now. can you paste the problematic snippet inline? link pls.

maria: sure https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4821 :eyes:

sam: skimmed. main issue: the python section says "async generator yields pages" but the code yields tokens. confuses the pagination doc. suggest we rename to "async stream of page objects" and add a tiny adapter example.

maria: good catch. current python snippet:
```
async def stream_response(client):
    async for token in client.stream("Hello"):
        yield token
```
will change to:
```
async def stream_pages(client):
    async for page in client.stream_pages("Hello"):
        for token in page.tokens:
            yield token
```
short and explicit.

yuki: for TypeScript I think we should show both `AsyncIterable<Token>` and the high-level `for await (const page of client.streamPages())` example. also include how retries surface: doc should warn that retries may duplicate page level events unless idempotent.

leo: Go example currently uses a single blocking receive on a channel and mixes cursor state in the same snippet — makes it look unsafe for concurrent callers. propose a small refactor to expose a `Cursor` type with `Next()` method.

sam: agree. propose adding this minimal Go example:
```
type Cursor struct { ch <-chan Page }
func (c *Cursor) Next(ctx context.Context) (Page, error) {
    select {
    case p, ok := <-c.ch:
        if !ok { return Page{}, io.EOF }
        return p, nil
    case <-ctx.Done():
        return Page{}, ctx.Err()
    }
}
```
notes: keeps concurrency clear.

maria: i also hit CI: docs site build failed on the new snippet linting (line length + gofmt). deploy-bot reported:
"deploy-bot: docs build failed — golangci-lint: file examples/go/cursor.go: gofmt: file not gofmted with -s"

yuki: i can fix formatting in the PR. also can add a tiny note about backpressure: "If your app cannot keep up, prefer pages over token streams to reduce syscall overhead."

sam: small editorial suggestion: under "Retries" section add a 1-line rule: "Retries should be idempotent at page boundaries; prefer opaque page tokens for stateful continuation." keeps it short.

leo: +1. also add an inline link to the SDK reference for `stream_pages()` and the Go Cursor type.

maria: okay i'll push a commit with the python rename, TS tweak, gofmt fix, and the editorial sentence. can someone approve after green CI?

yuki: i'll +1 after tests pass.

sam: i'll do a quick copyedit for clarity after the changes land.
